blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running IT as a business function means holding it to the same questions the business asks of any other team. What does IT deliver this year? How is its contribution measured? Which decisions does it own, which does it advise on, and which does it simply execute? When these questions have clear answers, IT stops being a mysterious cost centre and becomes a recognisable part of the company's results.

The finance, commercial and HR teams all have well-understood frames: budget, pipeline, headcount. IT needs its own. Systems stability, incident count, project delivery, security posture and user satisfaction are the everyday measures of whether IT is doing the job the business is paying for.

A senior leader who treats IT this way finds that conversations change. The CIO stops having to defend the team's existence and starts having the kind of conversation every other function already has: what are the priorities, what are the trade-offs, and what is the plan?

items.q: According to the text, what does running IT as a business function mean?
options: Keeping IT separate from the rest of the company
Cutting the IT budget every year
Holding IT to the same questions asked of any other team
Letting IT decide its own priorities alone
items.why: "holding it to the same questions the business asks of any other team."

items.q: Which of these is listed as an everyday measure of IT?
items.why: O texto cita "incident count" entre as medidas cotidianas de TI.

items.q: What happens to the CIO's conversations when IT is run this way?
options: The CIO reports only to the finance team
The CIO focuses only on cutting costs
The CIO stops defending the team's existence and discusses priorities and trade-offs
The CIO no longer attends board meetings
items.why: "The CIO stops having to defend the team's existence and starts having the kind of conversation every other function already has."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: IT deserves its own frame, just as finance has a budget.
IT's contribution should be measured, like any other function.
IT is a mysterious cost centre that cannot be measured.
Clear answers make IT a recognisable part of results.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta justamente que, com boas perguntas, TI deixa de ser um "centro de custo misterioso".

items.q: The comparison with finance, commercial and HR suggests that…
options: IT currently lacks the clear frame those teams already have
those teams do not need to be measured
IT is more important than the other teams
items.why: Inferência: "IT needs its own" implica que TI ainda não tem o quadro claro que os outros já possuem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James ajudando a nova CIO a montar o painel. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So here is what I am proposing for your first board meeting. We are not going to walk in with forty slides. We are building a dashboard with exactly five numbers, and every one of them answers a question the board already understands.

Right now I am sketching the first metric: system stability. The board does not care how the servers work, but they do care whether the platform is up when people need it. Second, incident count — how many things break each month, and whether that number is falling. Third, project delivery, so they can see what we are shipping this quarter against what we promised.

The fourth one is security posture, because every board is thinking about risk these days. And the fifth is user satisfaction, which tells you whether the people inside the company actually trust the tools.

Here is the thing. At the moment you spend most of your time defending the team. Once these five numbers are on the table, that conversation changes completely. You stop justifying that IT exists, and you start talking about priorities and trade-offs, exactly like finance does.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many numbers does James want on the dashboard?
items.why: "We are building a dashboard with exactly five numbers."

items.q: What does the board care about regarding system stability, according to James?
options: Whether the platform is up when people need it
items.why: "The board does not care how the servers work, but they do care whether the platform is up."

items.q: Why does James include security posture as a metric?
options: Because it is cheap to measure
Because every board is thinking about risk these days
Because the CIO asked for it
items.why: "security posture, because every board is thinking about risk these days."

items.q: What does James suggest the CIO currently spends most of her time doing?
items.why: Inferência: "At the moment you spend most of your time defending the team" — a situação atual que ele quer mudar.

items.q: What is the main change James expects the dashboard to bring?
options: The conversation shifts from justifying IT to discussing priorities
IT will need a larger budget
The CIO will report to the finance director
The board will stop meeting so often
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que a conversa deixa de ser "justificar que TI existe" e passa a ser sobre prioridades e trade-offs.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "IT is treated as a real business function, not a back office." A business function is…
options: a recognised part of the organisation with its own responsibilities
items.why: Business function = função de negócio: uma área reconhecida da empresa, com responsabilidades próprias.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The board wants to know what each team ___ this year, not just what it spends."
items.why: To deliver = entregar; o quadro quer ver o que cada time entrega.

items.q: "On this decision, IT does not own it — it only advises." To advise means to…
items.why: To advise = aconselhar: dar recomendação, sem necessariamente decidir.

items.q: "A mysterious cost centre is exactly what we are trying to avoid." This phrase describes a team that…
options: spends money in ways the business does not understand
items.why: Mysterious cost centre = centro de custo misterioso: gasta, mas o negócio não entende o valor.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every plan involves a ___ : more security usually means less convenience."
items.why: Trade-off = compromisso: ganhar de um lado custa algo do outro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando TI passa a falar a língua do negócio. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new dashboard." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the reporting model across all departments next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A few managers pushed back on reporting incident counts to the board." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They promised a security review but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Buying newer laptops will not move the needle on system stability." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
